name: Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Zayd al-Shaybānī
summary: The head of the Kufan grammarians in Baghdad and al-Mubarrad's rival for half a century; author of al-Faṣīḥ and of the Majālis, records of his teaching.
bio: Thaʿlab was born in Baghdad in 200/816, a client of Shaybān, and learnt al-Farrāʾ's books from his students, above all Salama ibn ʿĀṣim; al-Zubaydī places him alone in the fifth Kufan generation, 'the companions of Salama'. He knew al-Farrāʾ's books by heart and was famous for his memory of poetry and rare words.

For decades he and al-Mubarrad taught in the same city, and the ṭabaqāt are full of their rivalry: students passed between them, al-Zajjāj went over to al-Mubarrad, Ibn Kaysān and al-Akhfash al-Aṣghar heard both. Al-Zubaydī reports a judgement that Thaʿlab was as sparing of words as al-Mubarrad and wider in learning, but that he answered by hints, never plainly. His al-Faṣīḥ, a short list of the correct forms of common words, became one of the most commented books of the language, and his Majālis record what was said in his circle.
He became deaf in old age. The biographers tell that in 291/904, leaving the mosque with a book in his hand, he did not hear a horse behind him, was knocked into a ditch and died the next day.
